learningObjective: Diagnose why an autotuner's best-config picks differ across runs and identify the primary contributor.

canonicalClaims.claim: When measurement noise is on the same order as the runtime gap between top autotuner candidates, winner-take-all rankings are unstable across runs; robust methodology (more repetitions, median/geomean, equivalence bands) is required.
conditions: Measurement noise is characterized (variance across replays).
The tuner uses a winner-take-all rule.
nonImplications: Does not imply autotuning is unusable; sound methodology contains the issue.
Does not imply the top-2 gap is always within noise — for some workloads it exceeds noise.

misconceptions.claim: A GPU driver memory leak causes the non-determinism, and upgrading the driver fixes it.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Driver leaks manifest as monotonic slowdown or OOM, not as switching winners between two configs.

misconceptions.claim: Setting a fixed random seed makes different kernels report identical runtimes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Seeds control the tuner's exploration path; kernel runtimes depend on hardware state, not on the seed.

misconceptions.claim: Any two kernels that differ in runtime by less than 10% must have identical performance in practice.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The threshold depends on the measured noise floor; 10% may be entirely resolvable in low-noise contexts.

misconceptions.claim: Locking GPU clocks eliminates all measurement noise.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Clock locking removes DVFS jitter but not OS scheduling, memory allocator state, cache pollution.

implementationFacts: AutoTVM runs each config N times (default 3-5) and takes the median.
Ansor recommends a per-config minimum trial count and clock-locking for benchmarking.
performanceScenarios: On sm_80 without clock locking, single-kernel timing noise ranges 3-5% at 1 ms scale; below 100 µs, noise can exceed 10%.
